1.explanation: The key code elements involved are the Dropdown component and its render function in 'packages/react/src/components/Dropdown/Dropdown.js'. This is where the selected item is rendered in the button using 'itemToString(selectedItem)' for both the visual label and the title attribute. The bug arises because, for custom icon dropdowns, itemToString may return an object (for rendering an icon), leading to the '[object Object]' tooltip. The fix would likely involve modifying the Dropdown component to allow using 'itemToElement' (or a new prop) to render the selected item, not just the string representation, and to use a suitable string or label for the title attribute. No other classes or files in the compressed set are directly related to the rendering and logic for the Dropdown's selected item.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario is that when a custom Dropdown is used to select an icon (such as a warning icon), the selected item is rendered using itemToString, which works visually but results in the button's title attribute showing '[object Object]' instead of a user-friendly label or element. This is because itemToString is expected to return a string, but in the custom use case, it may return an object for rendering icons. The desired behavior is to allow the Dropdown to use itemToElement (or a similar prop) for rendering the selected item (including the button label and accessible title), not just the string conversion for the dropdown list items. The attached images show a tooltip with '[object Object]' instead of an appropriate description when hovering over the selected dropdown icon.

2.explanation: The Dropdown class/function in 'Dropdown.js' is responsible for rendering the dropdown UI and managing how selected items are displayed, including the button's title attribute. The bug arises specifically in the code where the title attribute of the dropdown button is set using itemToString(selectedItem). This does not work well for custom elements or objects, as it results in '[object Object]' being shown in the tooltip. To resolve the issue, the Dropdown component needs to provide a way (e.g., via a prop) to use itemToElement for rendering the selected item (and possibly the tooltip/title), instead of always using itemToString. The index.js file is only re-exporting and does not contain logic related to this bug.
2.bug_scenario: The bug scenario involves using a custom Dropdown component to select icons. When an item is selected, the dropdown button sets its title attribute using itemToString(selectedItem), which works well for strings. However, when items are objects (such as icon objects), itemToString returns an object, leading to the button's title attribute displaying '[object Object]' instead of a meaningful label or element. The attached images show dropdowns for selecting icons, with the last image illustrating the problematic tooltip displaying '[object Object]' over a selected icon.
